findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition breaks the emoji resize job
findings.description:
`self.downsize` is defined twice, and Ruby has no arity overloading, so the second definition (`from, to, dimensions, opts={}` at line 149) silently replaces the first (line 145). The only pre-existing caller, `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14`, calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with five arguments. That now raises `ArgumentError` (5 for 3..4), so every `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` run enqueued from `app/models/emoji.rb:73` fails and custom emoji are never downsized.

Lines 145-147 are dead code. Keep one signature and update the emoji job to pass `"100x100"`, or give the new method a distinct name.

findings.title: Existing JS test contradicts the new hardcoded limit
findings.description: "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded" sets `max_image_size_kb = 5`, validates a 10 KB image, and expects rejection with `{ max_size_kb: 5 }`. With `maxSizeKB` hardcoded to `10 * 1024` at `utilities.js:182`, a 10 KB file now passes, so both assertions fail. The test was not updated in this change.

findings.title: Client-side size check no longer honours attachment or admin limits
findings.description:
`validateUploadedFile` used `max_<type>_size_kb` for both images and attachments; it now uses a flat 10 MB for everything.

- **Attachments:** the server never downsizes them, so `max_attachment_size_kb` (1024 in the test settings fixture) is still enforced there. A user now uploads up to 10 MB before being rejected, instead of being stopped instantly in the browser.
- **Sites with higher limits:** a site that set `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10 MB is now capped at 10 MB client-side.
- **Wrong error text:** the 413 handler at `utilities.js:246` reports 10240 kb regardless of the real proxy or site limit.

Restrict the relaxed limit to `type === 'image'` and keep the site setting for attachments.

findings.title: Magic 10 MB constant duplicated across three sites and bypasses site settings
findings.description:
The same 10 MB literal appears at `uploads_controller.rb:55`, `utilities.js:182` and `utilities.js:246`, with no shared constant or setting. It is implicitly coupled to `client_max_body_size 10m` in `config/nginx.sample.conf:61`.

The API URL download previously respected `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`; it is now fixed at 10 MB even if the admin configured more or less. Every other `FileHelper.download` caller (`user_avatar.rb:22,66`, `pull_hotlinked_images.rb:9`) still uses the setting. Extract one named constant or site setting and expose it to the client.

findings.title: Downsize loop likely reads a stale size from the open tempfile
findings.description:
The loop condition and the `filesize` passed to `Upload.create_for` both use `tempfile.size`. `Tempfile#size` stats the open file descriptor, while `convert_with` rewrites the file by path and then runs `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` (`optimized_image.rb:164`), which in image_optim 0.20.2 replaces the file by rename as I recall it. I could not inspect the gem source here.

If so, the descriptor still points at the original inode and the size never appears to shrink. The loop would always run all five passes, shrinking dimensions to about 33%, and the original size is passed on, so `upload_validator.rb:84` still rejects the upload. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` in both places, as `Upload.create_for` already does with path-based access at `upload.rb:106,138`.

findings.title: Downsize result ignored and each pass re-encodes the image
findings.description:
The boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize` is discarded. If `convert` or `gifsicle` fails, the loop runs the same failing command five times with no log line and no early exit.

On success, each pass re-encodes the previous output, so a JPEG can go through five lossy generations. Computing a target ratio once from the current size versus the limit, and breaking on failure or no size reduction, would be both cheaper and higher quality.

findings.title: Animated GIFs are flattened or not reduced
findings.description:
Two paths misbehave for animated GIFs over the limit:

- **Browser uploads:** `optimize` picks the animated path only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (`optimized_image.rb:155`), but `from` is the tempfile path, not the original filename. The lockfile pins Rack 1.5.5, which as I recall creates extensionless multipart tempfiles; I did not verify the gem source. If so, the GIF goes through `convert #{from}[0]` (`optimized_image.rb:129`) and is stored as a single still frame.
- **API URL downloads:** the tempfile keeps its `.gif` extension, so `"80%"` is passed to `gifsicle --resize-fit` (`optimized_image.rb:120`). I believe that flag expects `WxH` and rejects a percentage (that would need `--scale`), so the command fails on each pass.

SVGs also match `FileHelper.is_image?` and would be fed to `convert`; `Upload.create_for` and `OptimizedImage.create_for` both special-case SVG, but this block does not.

findings.title: Up to five ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes on the upload path
findings.description: Each oversized image triggers up to five `convert` runs, each followed by a full `ImageOptim` pass, and `Upload.create_for` then runs orientation fix and ImageOptim again. This happens inline in the request for synchronous API calls, or inside the `Scheduler::Defer.later` block at `uploads_controller.rb:19`, where it delays other deferred work. Any logged-in user can trigger this with a file just under 10 MB. A single computed resize or a background job would bound the cost.

findings.title: No tests for the new downsizing behaviour or the changed `OptimizedImage` API
findings.description: No spec exercises the downsize loop: not the over-limit image being reduced, the image that cannot be reduced in five attempts, nor the GIF and SVG branches. There is also no spec covering `OptimizedImage.downsize`, `resize` or `optimize` after the signature change; a search for `downsize` under `spec/` returns nothing. A spec for `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` would have caught the FAIL above.

findings.title: Removing `OptimizedImage.dimensions` is safe within the repo
findings.description: A repo-wide search finds no remaining callers of `OptimizedImage.dimensions`. The 4-argument `resize` signature is preserved, so its callers (`upload.rb:98`, `letter_avatar.rb:48`, `uploads.rake:347`) are unaffected. Plugins outside this repo that call `optimize` or `dimensions` directly would break.

findings.title: Shell commands built by interpolation now take a new input shape
findings.description: `convert_with` runs `instructions.join(" ")` through backticks. This predates the change, and `upload.rb:162` already passes the same tempfile path to a shell. The change adds a free-form `dimensions` string to that command. Today it is only the literal `"80%"`, but the new 4-argument `downsize` accepts any string, so future callers must never pass user input. Using `Open3`/`system` with an argument array would remove the risk.
